title: Greek key border panel
subtitle: A framed rectangular panel with a continuous Greek key border in two colours on 13-count canvas
excerpt: The Greek key is one of the oldest border motifs in needlepoint. This small framed panel works a continuous Greek key border in dark wool on a cream background, all in basketweave tent stitch. Finished size is 15 by 20 cm.
sourceNotes: Greek key meander motif from Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), canvaswork borders chapter. Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), Greek border entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: A continuous geometric border motif of interlocking right-angle spirals, used in classical Greek and Roman decoration and in canvaswork borders since the Victorian era.

heroPrompt: A small framed needlepoint panel showing a Greek key border in dark navy on cream, mounted and framed in dark wood, natural light on a white shelf.

content.text: This panel works a continuous
Greek key meander

border in basketweave tent stitch on 13-count canvas. The design is 78 by 104 holes, finishing at 15 by 20 cm. The border is twelve holes wide; the centre is left as a plain fill or worked in a simple geometric pattern of your choosing.
What you need

items.label: Canvas
items.value: 13-count mono canvas, cut 26 by 31 cm (leaves a 5 cm margin around the 78 by 104 hole design area)

items.label: Thread A: border (dark)
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 838 / Anchor 1088 (very dark beige brown). About 12 m

items.label: Thread B: background (cream)
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 739 / Anchor 366 (ultra light tan). About 18 m

items.label: Frame
items.value: Scroll frame, 20 by 25 cm working area minimum

items.label: Frame
items.value: Picture frame with 15 by 20 cm aperture

content.text: Palette
Thread A: DMC 838 / Anchor 1088: very dark beige brown (border)
Thread B: DMC 739 / Anchor 366: ultra light tan (background)
Stretching the canvas
Mount the canvas on a scroll frame before starting. A frame this size benefits from the frame support throughout to reduce distortion in the large background areas.
Stitches used
Basketweave tent stitch
throughout.
Working method
The Greek key pattern is most easily
read from a counted chart
. Mark the canvas grid in pencil first: draw light lines every 10 holes to create a reference grid matching the chart squares.
Mark the outer boundary of the design (78 by 104 holes) with a basting thread.
Work the border motif first. Start at a corner and follow the Greek key line around the perimeter in Thread A. The key is twelve holes wide and follows a right-angle spiral repeating every 12 holes.
Once the border is complete, fill the background of the border with Thread B, using basketweave.
Fill the centre panel (54 by 80 holes) in Thread B, or work a chosen geometric fill in a third colour. Plain basketweave in the same cream gives a quiet, classical result.
Block the canvas after completion. Pin to size overnight.
Finishing
Lace the blocked canvas over a 15 by 20 cm acid-free mounting board. Fit into a picture frame without glass, or use a spacer strip to keep glass off the canvas surface.
What to try next
The same Greek key border on 18-count canvas at a smaller scale makes a smart bookmark or a repeating motif for spectacle case sides.
